verification.reason: The code path is real. `retire` removes a records-only folder whole (git-record-store.ts:286-292 via judgeFolder "clean" and withoutFolders). It leaves no mark. `add` (lines 190-199) only refuses a changeset with a disposal mark, so a stale host can write R1's records back into the retired changeset. The head decision admits this (line 50). Base rule 4 computes standing from the rounds that are present: a round stands unless a counted round names it as replaced. So if R2 is retired and R1 is re-added, R1 stands. The consequence is that an old passing round comes back and the blocking round that replaced it is gone. This also weakens the base promise that "no pointer for a writer to roll back". I did not trace the gate's standing code, nor whether a reopened pull request triggers a fresh review round. The chain needs several conditions: the pull request closed for 30 days or more, a late re-run of R1's records job, no re-add of R2, a reopen at the same head H, and no new round. A run against the gate would settle whether the gate really passes. I am leaving the severity as reported.
